explanation: Mass stays constant everywhere; weight (= mg) varies with local gravitational field. Answer C: mass constant, weight varies.

Adding controlled impurity to a semiconductor is called doping (not saturation, bonding, or amplification). Answer D.

Brownian motion: rapid, constant, irregular movement of particles (I); shows molecules exist (II); occurs in liquids AND gases, not only gases — so III is false; shows molecules in constant random motion (IV). Correct: I, II and IV. Answer D.

Total internal reflection conditions: (II) light travels from denser to less dense medium AND (III) angle of incidence exceeds critical angle. I is wrong (it says less to denser). Answer C: II and III only.

p-n junction diode allows current when forward-biased (low resistance) and blocks current when reverse-biased. Rectification works because it conducts in only one direction. Answer A.
Mass is the quantity of matter in a body — constant regardless of location (Earth or moon). Weight changes, not mass. Answer A.
Capillarity — rise or fall of liquid in a narrow tube — is caused by surface tension (interaction between liquid surface and tube walls). Answer B.
Below sea level, atmospheric pressure is higher. Higher external pressure raises the boiling point above 100°C. Answer A.

Transverse and longitudinal waves differ in the direction of particle vibration relative to wave travel. Transverse: perpendicular; longitudinal: parallel. Answer C.

Silicon and germanium both in Group IV; they form covalent bonds by sharing electron pairs. Answer B.
Smallest graduation on a metre rule = 1 mm. Least count (half smallest division) = 0.5 mm. Answer C.

Equilibrium condition under parallel forces: vector sum of all forces = zero (and sum of moments = zero). Answer B.
g on planet = 10/3 m/s². Weight = mg = 8 × (10/3) ≈ 26.7 N ≈ 27 N. Answer C.

Heat capacity of body = heat required to raise temperature by 1 K (total, not per unit mass). Answer A.

Compound microscope uses short focal length lenses for both objective and eyepiece to achieve high magnification. Answer C.
In normal adjustment (relaxed eye), final image of telescope is at infinity. Answer A.
Electrical energy for billing purposes is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Answer B.
Beta decay: neutron → proton + electron (β⁻). Atomic number increases by 1; mass number unchanged. Answer C.
At the magnetic equator, Earth's field is horizontal → angle of dip = 0°. Answer B.
²¹⁰₈₂Pb → ²⁰⁶₈₀Pb: mass decreases by 4, Z decreases by 2 → one alpha particle emitted. Answer B.
Newton (N = kg·m/s²) is a derived unit, not fundamental. Fundamental SI units include metre, ampere, and second. Answer C.
Neon gas in a discharge tube produces characteristic red/orange-red light. Answer D.
Two light nuclei (²₁X + ²₁X) combining to form heavier nucleus (³₂Y) with release of energy = nuclear fusion. Answer B.
Electromagnet strength increases with: more turns in coil, higher current, and softer core. Answer A: increases in number of turns.
Net movement of solvent through a semi-permeable membrane from high to low solvent potential = osmosis. Answer B.
Magnetic force on charge F = qvB sinθ. When velocity is parallel to field, θ = 0°, F = 0. Charge moves in straight line. Answer A.
Low humidity means air can absorb more water vapour → rate of evaporation from pool increases rapidly. Answer D.

Chemical energy (I) converts directly to light (chemiluminescence), and electrical energy (III) converts directly to light (in bulbs/LEDs). Sound (II) does not directly convert to light. Answer D: I and III only.
Image size/object size = image distance/object distance. Halving object distance doubles image size. Answer D: image is doubled.
Telescope is the instrument designed to view distant objects such as stars. Answer B.
Friction opposes motion, causing energy loss → reduces output work → efficiency decreases with increased friction. Answer B.
Two parallel plane mirrors facing each other produce infinite images (each image is reflected in the other mirror). Answer A.
Molecules of matter ARE in constant random motion (this is a core principle of kinetic theory). Statement III is NOT correct. Answer C.
Dynamo (generator) converts mechanical energy (rotation) into electrical energy. Answer A.
Semiconductors: conductivity increases with temperature (more electrons gain enough energy to cross the band gap). Answer B.
Saturated vapour pressure (SVP) increases with temperature — more molecules have enough energy to escape the liquid surface. Answer A.
Electromagnetic spectrum order (decreasing wavelength / increasing frequency): radio > microwave > infrared > visible > UV > X-rays > gamma. Gamma rays have shortest wavelength. Answer D.
Water waves are mechanical (require medium) and transverse (particles move perpendicular to wave travel). Answer A.
At absolute zero (−273°C = 0 K), molecular kinetic energy = 0, so gas pressure drops to zero. Answer B.
Relative density of liquid = density of liquid / density of water = upthrust in liquid / upthrust in water (by Archimedes). Answer B.
Shadows and eclipses occur because light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation) — objects block light paths. Answer B.
Saturated vapour: rate of condensation equals rate of evaporation — dynamic equilibrium. Answer B.
Electromagnetic waves (light, radio, X-rays) are transverse waves that do not require a medium. Answer A.
Boiling occurs when vapour pressure of liquid equals atmospheric pressure — bubbles form throughout liquid. Answer D.
Diagram-dependent question. Neutral point is where the resultant magnetic field is zero. Answer B (point X).
Atoms of different elements have different numbers of protons and different properties. They are NOT identical. Answer D.

All three statements are correct: positive charge = deficit electrons, negative charge = excess electrons, current = electron movement. Answer D.

²₁X + ²₁X → ³₂Z + ¹₀n + energy: two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus = nuclear fusion reaction. Answer A.
Shadows and eclipses form because light travels in straight lines — objects cast shadows. Answer D: rectilinear propagation.

Mirage: layers of air near hot road have varying refractive indices (I) and light bends (total internal reflection) so sky image appears on ground (III). I and III only. Answer A.

Evaporation = liquid turning spontaneously to vapour at any temperature (not just boiling point). Answer B.

Diagram-dependent (cooling curve). The flat region at 80°C = naphthalene's melting/solidification point. Answer C.
Diagram-dependent (resonance tube length = one wavelength). Answer C.

Upthrust = weight in air − apparent weight in liquid = 180 − 150 = 30 N. Answer C.

Heat from fire in closed room reaches distant person mainly by radiation (electromagnetic waves travel through air directly). Answer D.
Force on charged body in electric field: F = qE. Depends on charge q (I) and field intensity E (II). Mass has no effect. Answer C: I and II only.

Inductance is measured in Henry (H). Named after Joseph Henry. Answer D.

Two 2Ω resistors: series = 4Ω, parallel = 1Ω. Possible values: 1Ω or 4Ω. Answer D.
Normal adjustment: final image at infinity → foci of objective and eyepiece coincide between the lenses. Answer D.

Plane mirror: image is upright (erect), virtual (behind mirror), same size as object (magnification = 1). Answer D.

200 m: metre (fundamental). 24 s: second (fundamental). 8.3 ms⁻¹: derived (metre/second). Two fundamental, one derived. Answer D.
Henri Becquerel discovered natural radioactivity in 1896 while studying phosphorescence of uranium salts. Answer B.

Lead-acid accumulator: can deliver large current (low internal resistance) and can be recharged. Dry batteries can do neither efficiently. Answer C.

Energy = 0.75 kW × 24 h = 18 kWh. Cost = 18 × 65k = 1170k = N11.70. Answer B.

Pinhole camera: image/object height = image/object distance. 6/300 = d/750 → d = 6×750/300 = 15 cm. Answer C.

Gas molecules move randomly (not regularly). 'Molecules of gases are in regular motion' is NOT correct. Answer D.
Camera film records the image like the retina detects light in the eye. Both are at the back and receive focused light. Answer B.
ω = v/r = 12/1.5 = 8 rad/s. Answer C.

High PD in X-ray tube accelerates electrons to high kinetic energy. When they hit the anode target, X-rays are produced. Answer A.

Ampere is a fundamental SI unit (base unit for electric current). Joule, Newton, ohm, and watt are all derived units. Answer A.
After 2 s at 6 cm/s: object distance = 8 + 12 = 20 cm from mirror. Image is 20 cm behind mirror. Separation = 20 + 20 = 40 cm. Answer E.

Rutherford's model does not specifically apply to 'atoms with one electron' — that was Bohr's model refinement. Rutherford's model applies generally. Answer C.

Third-class lever: effort between fulcrum and load. Sugar tongs fit this (effort applied between hinge and load). Answer D.
d = v × t/2 = 330 × 4/2 = 660 m. (Echo travels to wall and back = 2d.) Answer B.

Young's modulus (stress/strain ratio) is only valid up to the elastic limit, beyond which permanent deformation occurs. Answer B.

'Steel is more magnetized than soft iron' is NOT correct. Soft iron is more easily magnetized (higher permeability), while steel retains magnetism longer (harder magnet). Answer A.
Two light nuclei combining to form heavier nucleus + energy = nuclear fusion. Answer B.
¹⁹⁸₇₉Au → ¹⁹⁸₈₀Hg: mass number unchanged, Z increases by 1 → one beta-minus particle emitted (neutron → proton + electron). Answer A.
Polarity of electromagnet (which end is N or S) determined by direction of current through the coil (right-hand rule). Answer D.
Heisenberg uncertainty principle: Δx·Δp ≥ h/4π. Simplified textbook form: Δx·Δp ≥ h. Answer C.
Diagram-dependent (micrometer reading). By key: reading = 2.46 mm. Answer B.
Surface phenomena occur at surfaces. Evaporation (surface), photoelectric emission (surface), thermionic emission (surface). Condensation is a bulk/volume process, not strictly surface. Answer A.
Diagram-dependent (circular motion vectors). Velocity is tangential; acceleration is centripetal (toward centre). Answer B: diagram II.
Diagram-dependent (pendulum KE vs displacement). KE is maximum at equilibrium (displacement=0) and zero at extremes. Answer B: diagram II.
Efficiency = (1 − fraction wasted) × 100 = (1 − 1/4) × 100 = 75%. Answer D.
Diagram-dependent (magnetic field pattern between bar magnets). Answer B: diagram II.
Diagram-dependent (fuse placement in iron circuit). Fuse must be on live wire, before the element. Answer C: diagram III.

By given key: only statement I is correct. Answer D. (Note: standard physics — gravitational potential ∝ 1/r, not r²; field strength is a vector; field intensity ∝ weight of unit mass. Key may be erroneous.)
Impedance = total opposition to AC in circuit (includes resistance and reactance). In C-R circuit, Z = √(R² + X_C²). Answer A.
AC transmitted at high voltage, low current: power loss = I²R. Lower I → much less heat loss in cables → economical transmission. Answer D.
Heisenberg uncertainty principle: complementary variables are position (x) and momentum (p): Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ/2. Answer C.
Diagram-dependent (mercury atom energy levels). Ionisation energy = energy to remove electron from ground state to infinity. By key: +10.4 eV. Answer B.
Nucleon number (mass number) = total protons + neutrons in nucleus. Answer D.
Diagram-dependent (EM spectrum table). By key: P = Visible, Q = Ultraviolet, R = X-ray. Answer A.
Gamma radiation can be used as radioactive tracer (gamma cameras in medicine) and is naturally present in background radiation. Answer D.
Diagram-dependent (density-temperature graph of water). Water density peaks at 4°C — graph shows maximum at 4°C. Answer C: diagram III.
Pitch depends on frequency (and factors affecting frequency: tension, mass, length of vibrating string). Amplitude affects loudness, not pitch. Answer D.
Diagram-dependent (three-pin plug wiring). By key: P=neutral, Q=earth, R=live. Answer B.
'Electrolyte does not need attention' — NOT an advantage; alkaline accumulator electrolyte (KOH) DOES need periodic checking. Answer A.
Standard resistor = resistor with precise, fixed, known resistance value used as reference. Answer B.
Induction coil produces high-voltage AC pulses — used for spark generation, X-ray tubes, discharge studies. NOT suitable for AC power transmission (uses transformers instead). Answer D.

Photoelectric effect applications: (I) automatic light switches at dusk — YES (light-dependent resistors/photoelectric cells); (II) automatic doors — YES; (IV) automatic voltage stabilizers — YES. (III) air conditioning switches use thermostats, not PE effect. Answer A: I, II and IV only.
Radioisotopes used in: medicine (tracers, cancer treatment), oil industry (pipeline tracing), agriculture (mutation breeding, pest control). NOT used in weather forecasting. Answer D.
Acceleration = rate of change of velocity = Δv/Δt. 'Time rate of increase of velocity' = acceleration. Answer C.
Momentum = mv, has both magnitude and direction → vector quantity. Volume, energy, and speed are scalars. Answer B.
Lenz's law: induced current direction opposes the flux change causing it. Named after Heinrich Lenz. Answer B.
Gold-leaf electroscope: degree of leaf divergence indicates amount of charge — can compare charge magnitudes on different bodies. Answer C.
Mechanical waves require a medium (waves in pipes, water waves, sound waves). Radio waves = electromagnetic waves → do not require medium. Answer C.
TIR requires: light going from dense to less dense medium AND angle > critical angle. Air to water: air is less dense than water → going from less dense to more dense → TIR cannot occur. Answer C.
At steady (constant) velocity: acceleration = 0 → net force = 0 (Newton's 1st law). Answer C.
Air introduced above mercury creates additional pressure above it → total pressure on mercury increases → mercury level drops. Answer B.
East-West placement ensures bar magnet is perpendicular to Earth's horizontal magnetic field → molecular magnets remain randomly arranged (not aligned by Earth's field). Answer A.
Speed of sound lowest in gases (least dense/elastic), higher in liquids, highest in solids. Air has lowest speed. Answer A.
Maximum-minimum thermometer records highest and lowest temperatures since last reset (not continuously). Answer D.
Soft iron loses magnetism readily → armature demagnetises quickly each cycle → allows electric bell to work (clapper released between strikes). Answer B.
AC generator → DC generator: replace slip rings with split-ring commutator (rectifies output). Answer D.
Capacitor stores electric charge (and electrical energy). Answer D.
Water anomalous expansion: from 0°C to 4°C, water contracts (density increases to maximum at 4°C). Answer B: 0°C to 4°C.
Connecting wires simply carry current — they are not safety devices. Earth wire, fuse, and switch are all safety devices. Answer A.
Area under velocity-time graph = displacement = distance (for motion in one direction). Answer D.
Kinetic energy is conserved only in perfectly elastic collisions (no deformation, no energy converted to heat/sound). Answer D.
Volume inversely proportional to pressure at constant temperature = Boyle's Law: PV = constant (T constant). Answer C.
C = ε₀εᵣA/d. Decreasing separation d → C increases (inversely proportional to d). Answer A.
Depolarizing agent in Leclanche cell = manganese(IV) oxide (MnO₂), which oxidises hydrogen to prevent polarization. Answer C.
Hot soapy water: soap reduces surface tension of oil (making it easier to wash off) and heat speeds up the process. Answer B.
Graphite moderator in nuclear reactor slows fast neutrons to thermal neutrons needed for sustained fission chain reaction. Answer C.
Telephone earpiece converts electrical signals to sound (pressure) waves via electromagnet moving a diaphragm. Answer A: electrical to sound.
Lift accelerating upward: apparent weight = m(g+a) = 60(10+5) = 60×15 = 900 N. Answer D.
Total resistance = V/I = 5/0.005 = 1000 Ω. R_meter = 1000 − 975 = 25 Ω. Answer C.
In magnetic field: alpha particles (charged) deflected, beta particles (charged) deflected, gamma rays (uncharged EM) NOT deflected. Answer B: deflected, deflected, not deflected.
Work done by friction = μmg × d = 0.22 × 500 × 8 = 880 J. Answer A.
g is larger at poles than equator (Earth is flatter at poles → closer to centre). T = 2π√(L/g): larger g → smaller T → faster oscillation. Answer D.
By given key: red light releases smaller number of electrons than green light. Answer B. (Note: number of photoelectrons depends on intensity; frequency determines KE of emitted electrons.)
Hydraulic press: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ (Pascal). F ∝ A = π d²/4 ∝ d². Answer A: F ∝ d².
AC generator → DC motor: replace slip rings with split-ring commutator AND connect a DC battery (to drive it as motor). Answer A.
Light going from less dense (air) to denser (water) medium: bends toward normal (refracts toward normal). Answer C.
Coulomb's law: F = kq₁q₂/r². Decreasing distance r → F increases (inversely proportional to r²). Answer B.
Diver falls: gravitational PE decreases (converts to KE). In absence of air resistance, total mechanical energy conserved (PE+KE = constant). Answer A: decrease in gravitational PE.
Luminous object = produces its own light (sun, fire, light bulb). Non-luminous = only reflects light. Answer B.
In photoelectric effect: number of electrons emitted per second ∝ intensity of incident radiation (more photons = more electrons). KE of electrons ∝ frequency. Answer A.
Joule (J = kg·m²·s⁻²) is derived from fundamental units. Metre, kilogram, candela are fundamental SI base units. Answer C.
Vacuum between double walls: eliminates air → no convection (no medium for air currents) and no conduction through air. Silver coating handles radiation. Answer B: convection and conduction.
Molecules of both solids and liquids exhibit vibratory motion (vibrate about mean positions). Gas molecules move freely. Answer D.
In transverse stationary wave, node to adjacent antinode = λ/4. Answer D.
Heating metal sphere: volume increases (thermal expansion), mass stays constant, density = m/V decreases. Answer C.
C = ε₀εᵣA/d. Increase C by: (I) decrease d — YES; (III) increase plate overlap area A — YES; (II) increase d — NO (decreases C); (IV) remove dielectric — NO (decreases C). Answer A: I and III only.
Acceleration = slope of velocity-time graph (Δv/Δt). Area gives displacement. Answer C.
Voltmeter = galvanometer + high-value resistor in series (multiplier). Limits current through galvanometer for given voltage. Answer D.
Heat in wire = I²Rt. To reduce heat, reduce resistance. R = ρL/A: increasing diameter (cross-sectional area A) reduces resistance. Answer B: greater diameter wire.
f = holes × rotations/sec → 480 = 20 × n → n = 24 rev/s. Answer C.
Half-life = 1 hr. 6am to 9am = 3 hours = 3 half-lives. Remaining = 200 × (1/2)³ = 25 g. Decayed = 200 − 25 = 175 g. Answer A.

Increasing voltage → current increases (I = V/R); more current → more heating → resistance and temperature increase. Answer C: current and temperature only (resistance is fixed, not changed by voltage directly).
In plane progressive wave, all points have the same amplitude (energy distributed uniformly). 'Neighboring points have different amplitudes' is NOT a characteristic. Answer B.
Ice cube heating from −5°C to 0°C (question likely means −5°C): Q = mcΔT = 20×2.1×5 = 210 J. Answer D.
Quality (timbre) of a note = characteristic determined by its overtone composition. Different instruments playing same pitch have different quality. Answer C.
In CRT, electrons produced by thermionic emission from heated metal filament (cathode). Answer A.
Distance is a scalar (magnitude only). Displacement is a vector (magnitude + direction). 'Distance is a vector' is NOT correct. Answer D.
High relative humidity: air already saturated with water vapour → less evaporation from skin → sweating less effective → feel hotter. Answer A: rate decreases.
Pascal's principle: pressure applied to enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid. Answer C.
Force (vector), displacement (vector), momentum (vector) — all three are vectors. Answer B.
Resistance R = ρL/A depends on resistivity (material), length, and cross-sectional area. Mass has no direct effect on resistance. Answer A.
